5+h|Turbulence
|Turbulence model +
_k-epsilon: Reynolds-averaged flow with the standard k-epsilon model (Elmer KESolver) and wall functions on No slip walls. Stationary studies, 2D and 2D axisymmetric._ | | |None (laminar flow) |None (laminar flow), k-epsilon
|Under-relaxation factor +
_Of the flow and of the turbulence solve in every segregated iteration. k-epsilon's fixed point is unstable, so both the turbulence and the flow solve are damped; Elmer's own references relax the turbulence solver at 0.5. A damping factor other than 1 in the study's Solver Configurations takes its place._ | | |`+0.5+` |Expression
|Segregated iterations +
_Largest number of flow and turbulence solves in turn. Segregated k-epsilon converges only tenths of a percent per iteration once wall functions are valid, so a well-posed turbulent case needs a few thousand iterations to reach Elmer's own 1e-4..1e-5 coupling tolerance. The study's Max coupling iterations applies instead when larger._ | | |`+2500+` |Integer
5+h|Elmer Solver
|Additional Elmer solver keywords +
_Lines appended verbatim to this interface's Solver section in the .sif file_ | | | |Text (multi-line)
